confirmed.title: Receipt family registered but never aggregated: no receipt lane in aggregate reconciliation (D5/D6 gap)
confirmed.detail: RECEIPT_CLAIM_REGISTRY declares required keys, arithmetic and line-item-sum invariants, and full aggregate projection metadata (aggregate_schema_name="receipt", required containers merchant/transaction), but AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"} and _reconcile_regions has no receipt branch, so maybe_reconcile_semantic_annotation returns None for schema_name="receipt" with canonical_target_schema="receipt". Consequences: (1) receipt documents (a first-class live schema in STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS) never get a canonical receipt aggregate document_extractions row; (2) cross-region claim reconciliation never happens for receipts — a total claim from the receipt_payment_summary region and a subtotal/line-items claim set from the receipt_line_item_table region are resolved per-region in claim_candidates.py but never resolved together, so the receipt total-arithmetic and line_item_sum invariants in the registry can effectively never fire across regions; (3) receipts never get a persisted quality outcome (see D8 finding). The receipt aggregate_* registry fields are dead data. Tests only cover receipt-shaped schemas re-targeted to service_record/retail_order observations (tests/unit/extraction/test_reconciliation_repository.py:315-387), never a true receipt aggregate.
confirmed.evidence: reconciliation_repository.py:36: AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"}; _reconcile_regions (lines 174-198) branches only on "invoice", "document_observation", "medical_eob" and returns None otherwise; _aggregate_schema_name (lines 201-210) returns None for schema "receipt" unless canonical_target_schema is retail_order/service_record. claim_registry.py:193-196 sets aggregate_schema_name="receipt", aggregate_line_items_key="line_items", aggregate_required_containers=("merchant", "transaction") which nothing consumes.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a receipt branch (a thin wrapper like medical_eob_reconciliation.py calling resolve_claim_regions_for_family(family="receipt") + project_claim_family_payload) and add "receipt" to AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS, or explicitly document/remove the receipt aggregate registry metadata if receipt aggregation is intentionally out of scope.

verdict.reasoning: Every evidentiary claim reproduces against the current working tree. reconciliation_repository.py:36 defines AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"}; _reconcile_regions (lines 166-198) branches only on those three and returns None otherwise; _aggregate_schema_name (lines 201-210) returns None for schema_name="receipt" with canonical_target_schema="receipt" because OBSERVATION_AGGREGATE_CANONICAL_TARGETS (line 37) covers only retail_order/service_record. The ADR 0005 Implementation Progress log records aggregate persistence for invoice, document_observation, and medical_eob only — no entry adds, defers, or substitutes a receipt aggregate lane, while validators (_receipt_checks), candidate_schema_policy ("receipt." prefix), and canonical_promotion_policy (receipt keys) are all receipt-ready, indicating omission rather than documented design. Tests at test_reconciliation_repository.py:306-387 cover only schema_name="receipt" retargeted to service_record observation aggregates, never a true receipt aggregate. The uncommitted diff touches only model_output_contract_boundary.py and is unrelated. Severity high is fair: one of exactly three first-class structured schemas gets no canonical aggregate document_extractions row, no cross-region invariant enforcement, and no aggregate quality outcome, while invoice and medical_eob get all three.

confirmed.title: D8 quality outcomes are metadata-only: no DB column, no API/UI surface, no_extraction_target unreachable, combiner dead
confirmed.detail: ADR D8 says the four quality outcomes are "persisted decisions". In the working tree the resolver computes them, but the only persistence is claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py:62 writing metadata["quality_outcome"] into the aggregate payload, which lands inside document_extractions.normalized_json->'metadata' (extraction_repository.py INSERT has no outcome column; grep of database/*.sql migrations finds zero occurrences of quality_outcome — no column on document_extractions or documents). No API route reads it: apps/api/structura_api routes (routes_documents.py, routes_review.py) expose review candidates and statuses but never the quality outcome. The only readers (build_document_quality/build_phase9_document_intake in lib/documents) are called exclusively from unit tests — no production caller. Additional gaps: (a) the outcome exists only for invoice/medical_eob/document_observation aggregates; receipt and any non-aggregated document have no outcome at all; (b) no_extraction_target is unreachable in production wiring — claim_resolver.py:125 emits it only when requested_family == "no_extraction_target", and every caller passes invoice/receipt/medical_eob/document_observation; when Qwen plans no_extraction_target (lib/semantic_annotations/service.py:79,92) no extraction rows are created so no resolver runs and nothing is persisted; (c) combine_quality_outcomes (quality_outcomes.py:22-25) has zero callers anywhere including tests — the intended document-level rollup never happens.
confirmed.evidence: claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py:62: metadata["quality_outcome"] = claim_projection.quality_outcome (only write path). extraction_repository.py:440-470 INSERT INTO document_extractions has no quality-outcome column. `grep -rn quality_outcome database/*.sql` returns nothing. `grep -rn build_phase9_document_intake` matches only tests/. claim_resolver.py:125: no_extraction_target=requested_family == "no_extraction_target" with no production caller passing that family. `grep -rn combine_quality_outcomes lib apps workers tests` matches only its definition.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a quality_outcome column (or documents-level rollup field) written at aggregate persistence and at plan completion for no_extraction_target documents; expose it via the documents/review API; wire combine_quality_outcomes into a document-level rollup or delete it.

confirmed.title: Review rerun_extraction action enqueues a document-level extract job that live routing always rejects
confirmed.detail: The user-facing review action `rerun_extraction` (reachable via POST /documents/{id}/review-actions) creates an `extract` job with no semantic_region_id and a target schema defaulting to "receipt" (lib/review/service.py:253). The worker passes semantic_region_id=None to ExtractionService.extract_document, so semantic_task is None, and ModelRoutingExtractionGateway raises ModelProtocolError("Live Granite extraction requires a grounded semantic region task. Broad document-level structured extraction is disabled.") for every structured schema in live mode. The fail-closed routing is correct per the ADR progress log (2026-06-06), but the rerun feature was never migrated: every user-requested re-extraction in production now fails operationally instead of re-running Smart Parse planning or re-enqueueing grounded region tasks. This converts a quality/review action into a guaranteed pipeline failure.
confirmed.evidence: lib/review/service.py:174-190 creates job_type="extract" via build_extract_document_job_payload without semantic_region_id; _target_schema_from_action (lines 245-253) returns "receipt" by default. routing.py:50-56: `if granite_requested: if semantic_task is None: raise ModelProtocolError("Live Granite extraction requires a grounded semantic region task...")` and schema "receipt" is in STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS (routing.py:21).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Change rerun_extraction to re-enqueue the semantic-annotation job (Smart Parse) for the document, or to re-enqueue the existing grounded region extract tasks for the current semantic annotation, instead of a broad document-level extract.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the current working tree. The rerun_extraction review action (lib/review/service.py:157-191) enqueues a document-level "extract" job via build_extract_document_job_payload with no semantic_region_id and target schema defaulting to "receipt" (lib/review/service.py:253). The worker passes semantic_region_id=None and defaults route_profile to "docling_plus_structured_extraction" (workers/extraction/worker.py:87-89, 106). ExtractionService._semantic_task_for_document returns None when semantic_region_id is None with no fallback resolution (lib/extraction/service.py:286-287), so semantic_task=None reaches ModelRoutingExtractionGateway, which raises ModelProtocolError because granite_requested is True via both the route profile (routing.py:18) and the structured schema set (routing.py:21, 47-55). Severity high is appropriate: a user-facing review action is a guaranteed pipeline failure in the production (live) configuration, with retry churn, though it does not corrupt data or admit ungrounded values (the fail-closed behavior itself is spec-correct).

confirmed.title: Aggregate reconciliation permanently stuck when any region job dead-letters or is cancelled
confirmed.detail: maybe_reconcile_semantic_annotation is only invoked from the extraction worker after a SUCCESSFUL extract job. Its trigger compares completed current region rows against _expected_region_job_count, which counts pipeline_jobs with NO status filter — failed, dead_letter, and cancelled jobs are all included. A region job that terminally fails never produces an extraction row, so len(rows) < expected_count holds forever and the document-level aggregate (canonical invoice/EOB/observation facts, aggregate review task) is never built, even though every other region succeeded. There is no sweeper, no compensating review task, and plan tasks are never marked failed. This is made highly likely in production by extraction_failure_policy: a single Granite ModelTimeoutError on route docling_plus_granite_structured returns retryable=False, dead-lettering the job on its FIRST attempt. The semantic worker's cancel-cascade (workers/semantic_annotations/worker.py:107-116) produces the same permanent block via cancelled jobs.
confirmed.evidence: _expected_region_job_count: "SELECT COUNT(*) ... FROM pipeline_jobs WHERE document_id = %s AND job_type = 'extract' AND payload_json ->> 'semantic_annotation_id' = %s AND payload_json ->> 'target_schema_name' = %s" (no status predicate); trigger: "if expected_count == 0 or len(rows) < expected_count: return None"; model_failure_policy.py: "if isinstance(exc, ModelTimeoutError) and route_profile == 'docling_plus_granite_structured': return ExtractionFailurePolicy(retryable=False, policy='do_not_retry_timeout')"; jobs/service.py:405: "if current['attempt_count'] >= current['max_attempts'] or not retryable: status = 'dead_letter'".
confirmed.suggestedFix: Count only jobs that can still produce rows (exclude dead_letter/cancelled) and reconcile when all remaining jobs are terminal, emitting a partial aggregate with needs_human_review plus an explicit missing-region decision; alternatively trigger reconciliation from the dead-letter/cancel path as well.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against working tree. (1) maybe_reconcile_semantic_annotation is called only from workers/extraction/worker.py:129 on the success path of an extract job; the exception path (worker.py:168-180) just calls fail_job with no reconciliation, no plan-task failure marking, and no compensating review task — grep shows no other production caller and no sweeper anywhere in lib/, workers/, apps/. (2) _expected_region_job_count (lib/extraction/reconciliation_repository.py:220-228) counts pipeline_jobs with no status predicate, so dead_letter and cancelled jobs inflate expected_count; payload keys semantic_annotation_id/target_schema_name match build_extract_document_job_payload (lib/jobs/event_payloads.py:53,58). (3) _current_region_extraction_rows (reconciliation_repository.py:242-259) requires status='completed' is_current semantic_region rows, which terminally failed jobs never produce, so the gate at lines 67-68 (len(rows) < expected_count -> return None) blocks the aggregate forever. (4) The terminal state is realistic on the active route: region jobs are enqueued with route_profile='docling_plus_granite_structured' (lib/semantic_annotations/service.py:246,318), extraction_failure_policy returns retryable=False for ModelTimeoutError on that route (model_failure_policy.py:21-25), and fail_job dead-letters non-retryable failures on the first attempt (lib/jobs/service.py:404-406). (5) claim_next_job_record claims only ('queued','failed') (service.py:309); dead_letter/cancelled jobs are recoverable only via the manual admin retry_job endpoint (service.py:553-585). The semantic worker cancel-cascade (workers/semantic_annotations/worker.py:107-116) creates counted cancelled jobs the same way. (6) The ADR 0005 Implementation Progress log (through the 2026-06-06 entries) contains no fix for this; its 'retry once -> pipeline_failed' fail-closed policy entry (lines 462-467) institutionalizes first-attempt dead-lettering on Granite structured-output/timeout failures. Net effect: one Granite timeout on one region permanently and silently suppresses the document-level canonical aggregate (invoice/medical_eob/document_observation) and its review task even when all other regions succeed, with only unprompted manual operator retry as recovery. Minor caveat: the cancelled-job variant is arguably intended abandonment of the whole annotation run, but the dead-letter variant alone sustains the finding. Critical severity is warranted for silent permanent loss of the pipeline's document-level canonical output under a common failure mode.

confirmed.title: Receipt family has no aggregate reconciliation despite being a first-class target schema with declared aggregate registry metadata
confirmed.detail: AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {invoice, medical_eob, document_observation} and OBSERVATION_AGGREGATE_CANONICAL_TARGETS = {retail_order, service_record}. A plain receipt document (schema_fit selects target_schema 'receipt' when Docling anchors fit; canonical_target_schema 'receipt') returns None from _aggregate_schema_name, so no document-level reconciliation ever runs. Consequences: receipt claims from different regions (payment-summary totals vs line-item table) are never co-resolved, so the registered receipt line_item_sum invariant (claim_registry.py:163) and cross-region conflict resolution required by D6 cannot fire end-to-end; no canonical receipt.v1 aggregate payload, aggregate review task, or document_rollups receipt totals are produced via the aggregate path. Perversely, WEAK receipts that schema_fit downgrades to document_observation DO get an aggregate, while well-anchored receipts get none. The receipt registry already declares aggregate_schema_name='receipt' (claim_registry.py:193), showing the projector data exists but the wrapper/trigger wiring is missing.
confirmed.evidence: reconciliation_repository.py:36: AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"}; _reconcile_regions has branches only for invoice/document_observation/medical_eob and returns None otherwise; classification.py:10: TARGET_EXTRACTION_SCHEMAS = {"receipt", "invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"}; claim_registry.py:193: aggregate_schema_name="receipt".
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add 'receipt' to AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS and a receipt branch in _reconcile_regions using resolve_claim_regions_for_family(family='receipt') + project_claim_family_payload, mirroring the invoice wrapper.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the current working tree. reconciliation_repository.py:36 omits "receipt" from AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS, _aggregate_schema_name (lines 201-210) returns None for schema_name="receipt"/canonical_target_schema="receipt" (contract_registry.py:219-236 confirms plain receipts get canonical target "receipt"), and _reconcile_regions (166-198) has no receipt branch. The worker (workers/extraction/worker.py:129-138) is the only document-level claims-pooling trigger, and no receipt reconciliation module exists anywhere. Receipts genuinely take the multi-region path (contract_registry.py:26-32 plans separate receipt_payment_summary and receipt_line_item_table Granite jobs), so payment-summary totals and line-item-table claims are never co-resolved by the D6 resolver, no receipt.v1 aggregate payload or aggregate review task is ever produced, and the registry's declared aggregate metadata (claim_registry.py:193-196) is consumable by the generic projector (claim_projection.py:12-46) but never wired. The perverse asymmetry holds: schema_fit.py:172-179 downgrades weak receipts to document_observation which DOES aggregate, while well-anchored receipts (schema_fit.py:162-171) get nothing. The ADR 0005 log records aggregate support for invoice/document_observation/medical_eob/service-retail-observation but never receipt, and never declares receipt aggregates out of scope; no receipt-aggregate work exists in recent commits or the uncommitted diff. Two mild mitigations that temper but do not refute: (1) the receipt line_item_sum invariant can still fire within the line-items region alone because granite_receipt_line_items.v1 carries its own totals block — only the cross-region (payment-summary vs line-item table) check is impossible; (2) receipt canonical fields and document rollups can still be populated via per-region candidate promotion (canonical_repository.py:246-318), so receipts are not fact-less — the missing piece is document-level co-resolution, conflict precedence across regions, and the aggregate payload/review artifacts. These nuances are consistent with the finding's careful wording ("via the aggregate path", "end-to-end"). Given receipt is a first-class family with a published receipt.v1 app contract and the D6/D7 document-level deterministic reconciliation centerpiece never runs for it while weaker documents get one, high severity is appropriate.

confirmed.title: Claim anchor/group identity includes semantic_region_id, defeating cross-region dedupe; overlapping Qwen/Docling regions duplicate line items in canonical aggregates
confirmed.detail: ADR 0005 defines claim identity as hash(document_id, anchor, canonical_key, typed_value) with anchor = {page, docling_element_ids[], bbox, text_span} and dedupe 'never raw text'. The implementation adds semantic_region_id to ClaimAnchor.as_json(), and _group_id/_claim_id hash that JSON, so the SAME Docling table row extracted via two different semantic regions yields different claim_ids and different line-item group_ids — the resolver's 'structural row identity' collapse only works within one region. The invoice aggregate's second-pass _dedupe_line_item_dicts also keys on semantic_region_id (reconciliation.py:120), so duplicates survive into the canonical invoice payload, inflating line items (and at best demoting subtotal via line_item_sum_conflict). Overlap is reachable: _dedupe_equivalent_regions runs at manifest-normalization time using the UN-repaired granite_task (e.g., Qwen says 'kvp' for a line-item table; repair to 'tables_json' happens later in _region_for_granite_job at plan time), so a Qwen line-item region and the Docling-structural region for the same table both survive; the planner's _dedupe_key additionally includes region_source/coverage_role metadata so it never collapses across sources, and both land in the 'line_item' bucket (limit 4) producing two Granite jobs for the same table.
confirmed.evidence: claims.py ClaimAnchor includes 'semantic_region_id: str | None'; as_json emits it; _group_id = sha256({document_id, anchor: anchor.as_json(), [ordinal]}); ADR lines 62/65: anchor contract '{ page, docling_element_ids[], bbox, text_span }' and line 81: 'Fingerprint (document_id, anchor, canonical_key, typed_value)'. manifest_normalization._region_key includes region.granite_task (line 677) but corrected_granite_task_for_semantic_type is applied only in service.py:_region_for_granite_job; extraction_plan._dedupe_key includes spec.region.metadata.get('region_source').
confirmed.suggestedFix: Exclude semantic_region_id from anchor identity hashing (keep it as evidence/lineage only), and run _dedupe_equivalent_regions after granite-task/target-schema repair (or include the repaired task in the planner dedupe key without region_source).

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the working tree. (1) Identity: lib/extraction/claims.py:44 adds semantic_region_id to ClaimAnchor, as_json() emits it (claims.py:57), and both _group_id (claims.py:430-437) and _claim_id (claims.py:449-463) hash anchor.as_json() — so the same Docling table row extracted via two semantic regions yields distinct claim_ids and line-item group_ids, contradicting ADR 0005 lines 62/65/81 (anchor = {page, docling_element_ids[], bbox, text_span}; fingerprint (document_id, anchor, canonical_key, typed_value)). No ADR Implementation Progress entry removes region id from identity; the 2026-06-06 'structural row identity' and 'canonicalize element IDs' entries fix ordinal/order issues only. (2) Duplication survives: claim_resolver.py:143 groups line items by group_id, and reconciliation.py:120 (_line_item_locator_key) keys the invoice aggregate dedupe on semantic_region_id from the selected evidence ref (evidence_locator.py preserves it; claim_resolver.py:351-352 _clean_evidence keeps it), so content-identical duplicate rows survive into the canonical invoice payload. (3) Reachability: I attempted to refute via docling_targets.py:181-201 (injector skips tables already covered by table-grounded regions), but service.py:154-155 shows augmentation runs BEFORE normalization — a page-grounded Qwen line-item region (the exact case _normalize_table_grounding at manifest_normalization.py:202-233 exists to repair) does not block injection, then is retargeted to the same table. _dedupe_equivalent_regions (manifest_normalization.py:636-670) requires an exact _region_key match including the UN-repaired granite_task (line 677); repair happens only at plan time (service.py:511-523, task_routing.py:47-58), and tables_html/tables_otsl never match Docling's hard-coded tables_json (docling_targets.py:309) and are never repaired. The planner _dedupe_key (extraction_plan.py:380-382) includes granite_task, region_source, and coverage_role so Qwen/Docling specs never collapse; both land in the line_item bucket (extraction_plan.py:288-289, limit 4, per-page 3) yielding two Granite jobs over the same table. evidence_context.py:82 and evidence_concretizer.py:79-80 stamp each job's region UUID into every evidence ref; reconciliation_repository.py:61-88 loads all region rows and claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py:20-72 pools claims with no cross-region dedupe. Net effect: duplicated line items in the canonical invoice aggregate, a false line_item_sum_conflict demotion of a correct subtotal, and canonical output that varies with stochastic Qwen plan fan-out — violating D1/D7 and the 'identical Docling structure yields identical canonical JSON' consequence. One mitigating fact found: reconciliation_repository.py:263-274 (_force_aggregate_review) forces needs_review=True on every region aggregate, so duplicates never ship silently as clean — but the canonical payload, invariant decisions, and repeatability identity are still corrupted, so high severity stands for an extraction-accuracy product.

confirmed.title: Planner fanout caps silently drop must-extract/continuation line-item regions; aggregates never reflect the dropped coverage
confirmed.detail: plan_granite_jobs enforces hard_limit=6 tasks/document, per_page_limit=3, and bucket_limits {'line_item': 4, ...}; MAX_DOCLING_STRUCTURAL_TARGETS=4 caps Docling table targets. A multi-page invoice/EOB whose line-item table continues across >4 pages (each page a separate region, continuation_group metadata preserved but never consulted by the planner) gets at most 4 line-item Granite tasks; the rest are dropped with only a 'dropped_must_extract_target' warning and persisted plan-task status 'skipped_budget_exceeded'. Nothing downstream consumes those drops: _expected_region_job_count counts only created jobs, the aggregate is assembled solely from extracted regions, and resolver quality outcome looks only at claims — so the canonical aggregate silently omits entire pages of line items (it can even be 'clean' when no subtotal claim exists to trip line_item_sum_conflict). Cross-window continuation tables are exactly the documents that hit these caps.
confirmed.evidence: extraction_plan.py: 'hard_limit = 6; per_page_limit = 3; bucket_limits = {"line_item": 4, ...}'; dropped specs only append warnings ('dropped_must_extract_target:...'); dropped_task_status_and_reason -> 'skipped_budget_exceeded'; reconciliation_repository builds RegionExtraction only from document_extractions rows and never queries semantic_extraction_plan_tasks.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Either raise/scale caps with continuation-group awareness (treat a continuation group as one logical task or budget unit), or propagate planner drops into reconciliation so aggregates with skipped must-extract regions are forced to needs_human_review/insufficient_signal with an explicit coverage decision.

verdict.reasoning: Every load-bearing claim reproduces from the working tree. extraction_plan.py:126-134 hard-codes hard_limit=6, per_page_limit=3, bucket_limits line_item=4; dropped must-extract specs only append a 'dropped_must_extract_target' warning (184-189) and persist as 'skipped_budget_exceeded' plan tasks (202-208, extraction_plan_repository.py:74-82). docling_targets.py:25/199/227-239 caps Docling structural targets at 4. The planner never references continuation_group (it is preserved in region metadata via manifest_merge.py:52,63 but consumed only by visual_input_planning for within-task crops), so cross-page continuation tables get no budget relief. Jobs are enqueued only for plan.selected (service.py:233-234, 304-305), so reconciliation_repository.py's _expected_region_job_count (213-232) counts only created jobs and the aggregate assembles solely from completed document_extractions (235-260) — semantic_extraction_plan_tasks is never consulted by reconciliation; the only consumers of skipped_budget_exceeded are reliability telemetry counters (reliability_summaries.py:259-264). The resolver quality outcome derives only from claim decisions (claim_resolver.py:234-249) and the line_item_sum invariant is skipped when no subtotal claim exists (claim_invariants.py:183-186), so quality_outcome can be 'extracted_cleanly' while entire pages of line items are missing from the canonical aggregate. ADR 0005's Implementation Progress log has no entry addressing planner fanout budgets or dropped must-extract coverage, so this is not already fixed. Two caveats that temper but do not refute: (1) the fill pass (extraction_plan.py:168-178) can select line-item specs past the bucket cap up to the hard limit of 6, so 'at most 4' is strictly 'at most 6, typically 4 under competition' — tables spanning >6 pages still always lose regions; (2) _force_aggregate_review (reconciliation_repository.py:107, 263-274) forces needs_review=True on every aggregate, so the document always lands in review — but the review reason is generic, no missing-coverage signal reaches the aggregate or reviewer, and the canonical line-item facts genuinely omit dropped pages. The core defect — deterministic, unsignaled loss of line-item coverage on multi-page documents — holds, and these are exactly the core families (invoice/EOB) the pipeline targets, so high severity stands.

confirmed.title: Distinct line items collapse into one group when rows share the region-level anchor (silent row loss + cross-row field mixing)
confirmed.detail: _group_id() omits the ordinal whenever _anchor_has_row_identity() is true, and that predicate counts docling_element_ids or bbox as row identity. But evidence_ref_from_context() stamps the REGION's element_id and bbox onto every line item's evidence ref, and the Granite contracts allow row_index/table_id/page_number to be null per item. So whenever Granite returns null row_index (typical for receipts and visual-crop tables where Docling has no table grid), every row gets an identical ClaimAnchor, every row gets the same group_id, and _resolve_line_items merges all rows into one line item. Field winners inside the merged group are chosen per-field by JSON-string sort of typed_value, so the surviving row can pair one physical row's description with another row's amount. N-1 rows vanish from the canonical projection and candidates. This is the exact 'rows merged that shouldn't be' failure, reachable from fully contract-valid model output.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced end-to-end through normalize_granite_region_output -> envelope_from_normalization_projection -> claims_from_region_envelope -> resolve_claims_for_family with a schema-valid granite_receipt_line_items.v1 payload of 3 items (COFFEE 3.50 / BAGEL 2.25 / ORANGE JUICE 4.00, all row_index=null) and an EvidenceContext carrying the region element_id+bbox: output was 'line-item claims: 9 distinct groups: 1; projected line items: 1; merged: {amount: 2.25, description: BAGEL, quantity: 1.0}'. Code: claims.py:440-446 `return (anchor.row_index is not None or bool(anchor.docling_element_ids) or anchor.bbox is not None or anchor.text_span is not None)` -- region-level element/bbox satisfies this; claims.py:430-437 then drops the ordinal from the group hash.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Only treat an anchor as row-identifying when it is row-scoped: require row_index, or an element_id/bbox that differs from the region-level evidence context (e.g. compare against the envelope/region anchor, or always include ordinal unless row_index is present). Alternatively include source_text or ordinal in the group key when all sibling rows share an identical anchor.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the current working tree by exact code reading and an executed end-to-end repro. claims.py:430-437 drops the model ordinal from the line-item group hash whenever _anchor_has_row_identity (claims.py:440-446) is true, and that predicate accepts docling_element_ids or bbox alone. evidence_concretizer.py:85-96 stamps the REGION's element_id and bbox identically onto every line item's evidence ref, and line_item_provenance.py:14-27 only adds row_index when Granite supplies it; granite_receipt_line_items.v1.schema.json:98-104 permits row_index=null. The only regression test (tests/unit/extraction/test_claims.py:470-519) covers true duplicates with the same row_index=3, not distinct rows sharing a region anchor. One nuance: in the repro the merged group's conflicting values emitted needs_review decisions (source_precedence_conflict, line_item_sum_conflict), so the document is review-flagged rather than promoted cleanly — but the row loss itself is never surfaced (the projection/candidates show one merged item with no trace of dropped rows), and receipts with repeated identical line items merge with accepted/multi_source_agreement, i.e., fully silent loss. confirmed.title: money_value() fabricates currency "USD" for every amount; Granite contracts contain no currency field at all
confirmed.detail: money_value() returns {"amount": ..., "currency": value.get("currency") or "USD"} and {"amount": amount, "currency": "USD"} for scalars. grep over contracts/model_outputs/*.schema.json shows no contract declares a currency property, so every money value flowing through normalization -> envelope facts -> Claims is asserted as USD regardless of the document. It also renders the cross_field_currency_conflict invariant unreachable for contracted outputs (everything is uniformly USD), so the currency-conflict demotion path is dead in practice.

End-to-end repro projected transaction fields as {'subtotal': {'amount': 9.75, 'currency': 'USD'}, ...} from a payload that never stated a currency. `grep -rn currency contracts/model_outputs/` returns nothing.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Emit Money without currency when the source did not state one (claims._typed_value already supports currency-less money), or add a currency field to the Granite contracts so the model can assert it from the document. Treat document-level currency inference as a separate deterministic enrichment with its own provenance.

confirmed.title: String money parsing breaks accounting negatives and comma-decimal locales (sign flips and 100x-1000x magnitude errors)
confirmed.detail: All Granite money fields are typed ["number","string","null"], so string amounts are contract-valid and routinely reach number_value()'s regex `-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?`. Demonstrated failures: "(125.00)" -> +125.0 and "125.00-" -> +125.0 (accounting negatives lose their sign -- discounts/EOB adjustments flip from credit to charge); "1.234,56" -> 1.234 (European thousands-dot/decimal-comma off by ~1000x); "12,34" -> 1234.0 (decimal comma off by 100x). These wrong typed values become anchored Claims, pass admission, feed arithmetic invariants (causing both false demotions and false passes), and land in canonical output. The same regex lives in candidate_value_parsing.number_value used for quantities.

confirmed.title: Invoice aggregate fabricates totals.total from amount_paid, contradicting the resolver's own 'absent' decision
confirmed.detail: reconcile_invoice_region_extractions does `if "total" not in totals and "amount_paid" in totals: totals["total"] = totals["amount_paid"]`. amount_paid comes from the granite_payment_summary.v1 region (a payment record), not the invoice total. Scenario: invoice total $500 with a partial payment of $200; the line-items region fails to yield a usable invoice.total_amount claim but the payment-summary region yields amount_paid=200. Canonical output then asserts totals.total = $200 while metadata.claim_resolution_decisions simultaneously records invoice.total_amount decision=absent/required_claim_absent. This is a deterministic value fabrication outside the Claim path -- the projected total has no claim, no anchor of its own, and is wrong whenever the invoice is not exactly fully paid. It also defeats the required-key gate (total appears present in the payload even though no total claim exists).
confirmed.evidence: reconciliation.py:57-58: `if "total" not in totals and "amount_paid" in totals:\n        totals["total"] = totals["amount_paid"]`. Resolver registry declares invoice.total_amount as required (claim_registry.py:81) and emits absent decisions (claim_resolver.py:204-219); nothing reconciles that decision with the copied value.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Remove the copy. If a balance-due/amount-paid heuristic is desired, record it as an explicitly-labeled derived field with a reason code, never as totals.total.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the working tree. reconciliation.py:57-58 copies totals["amount_paid"] into totals["total"] when no total exists. Partial mitigations exist — the absent decision forces quality_outcome=needs_human_review, _force_aggregate_review marks validation needs_review, and canonical_promotion_policy.py:24-36 requires concrete evidence for .total_amount candidates so silent auto-promotion is likely blocked — but the canonical invoice.v1 aggregate still asserts a fabricated, claim-less total with the missing-total signal suppressed, so the finding stands at high severity as an extraction-accuracy/spec-conformance bug.

confirmed.title: PARTIALLY FIXED: Duplicate line items still survive across region boundaries because semantic_region_id is part of Claim/anchor/group/dedupe identity
confirmed.detail: The 2026-06-06 fixes (shared deterministic evidence-locator selection, structural row group IDs, canonical element-ID ordering) eliminate WITHIN-region duplicate survival from reordered/equivalent evidence arrays — that part is genuinely fixed. But cross-region duplication remains structurally possible: evidence_ref_from_context stamps every evidence ref with the region's semantic_region_id, _anchor_from_ref copies it into ClaimAnchor, and ClaimAnchor.as_json() emits it. Since claim_id, line-item group_id (claims.py:430-437 hashes anchor.as_json()), candidate dedupe keys (candidate_deduplication.py:144), and the invoice aggregate dedupe key (reconciliation.py:120) all include that anchor JSON, the SAME Docling table row extracted by two different semantic regions produces two distinct group IDs and two line items in the canonical aggregate. The plan/intent dedupe does not close this: extraction_plan._dedupe_key keys on semantic_type, granite_task, region_source, and coverage_role, so two regions over the same table with different semantic_type labels (a known Qwen cross-window drift mode) or a Docling-injected structural region plus a model region both dispatch. Duplicated rows then also break the line_item_sum invariant (spurious needs_review) or double-count canonical amounts. This also diverges from ADR 0005, whose anchor contract is { page, docling_element_ids[], bbox, text_span } and whose identity rule is fingerprint(document_id, anchor, canonical_key, typed_value) — region identity is not part of the spec anchor.
confirmed.evidence: claims.py:46-61 ClaimAnchor.as_json() includes ("semantic_region_id", self.semantic_region_id); claims.py:430-437 _group_id hashes {"document_id":..., "anchor": anchor.as_json()}; reconciliation.py:116-127 _line_item_locator_key starts with normalized_text_key(first.get("semantic_region_id")); extraction_plan.py:376 'page_level_intent = tuple(spec.region.expected_fields)' only when element_id and table_id are None, while the key includes spec.region.semantic_type and coverage_role so same-table regions with different labels both survive.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Exclude semantic_region_id from the anchor used for claim_id/group_id hashing and from candidate/aggregate dedupe locator keys (keep it as lineage on evidence only), per the ADR anchor contract. Optionally add a structural-grounding (table_id/element_id) component to the plan dedupe key independent of semantic_type/coverage_role.

Confirmed against the working tree; every cited line matches and no ADR 0005 log entry through 2026-06-06 addresses cross-region identity.

Impact confirmed: claim_invariants.py:174-217 sums the duplicated resolved line items against the selected subtotal — duplicates double the sum, demoting it to needs_review with line_item_sum_conflict (spurious review); with no subtotal claim, duplicated rows flow into the canonical aggregate unflagged (double-counting). confirmed.title: Live text-embedding client sends non-TEI payload to /embed and only falls back on 404/405, so the compose-documented TEI service fails with 422
confirmed.detail: EmbeddingHttpClient.embed posts {"model", "input": [...], "dimensions": ...} to /embed first, and only retries /v1/embeddings when the error message contains 'HTTP 404' or 'HTTP 405'. The configured live text-embed service is TEI (ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:cuda-1.9), whose native /embed route requires an "inputs" key — the client payload deserializes to HTTP 422, which is raised as ModelProtocolError without ever trying the OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings route that the live probe script actually validated (scripts/gpu/probe_phase8_5_live_models.py:146-151 posts to /v1/embeddings). This is currently masked because the resident bring-up never starts model-embed or worker-embeddings, but it blocks ever enabling the 'search' profile in live mode.

Mitigations (deterministic behavior, review_required=True, Qwen-never-canonical invariant intact) reduce value-fabrication risk but do not change the spec violation; severity high is appropriate given the gap spans four modules in the live path, hides Granite fanout policy in per-family term lists, and discards model-emitted table-grounded regions.

confirmed.title: Quality outcomes and claim decisions/reason codes are persisted but exposed by no API route, so the review UI cannot show them
confirmed.detail: ADR 0005 D8 makes quality outcomes (extracted_cleanly, needs_human_review, insufficient_signal, no_extraction_target) first-class persisted decisions, and the resolver emits per-key decisions with machine-readable reason codes (required_claim_absent, cross_field_arithmetic_conflict, cross_field_currency_conflict, line_item_sum_conflict, cross_field_plausibility_conflict). claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py writes both into the aggregate extraction metadata ('claim_resolution_decisions', 'quality_outcome'). But the document-detail SQL for document/aggregate-scope extractions selects neither metadata_json nor normalized_json (read_model.py:88-114) and _extraction_payload omits them, the review routes expose only review_tasks/field_candidates/canonical_fields, and grep shows zero occurrences of qualityOutcome or any outcome vocabulary anywhere in apps/api or apps/web/src. A reviewer therefore cannot see the document's resolver outcome, why a key was demoted to needs_review, or which decision/reason backs a candidate — the central explanation data the deterministic pipeline was built to produce. lib/documents/analysis_quality.py reads quality_outcome but only for the Phase 9 intake seam, not the API.

confirmed.suggestedFix: Include metadata_json (or a projected subset: quality_outcome, claim_resolution_decisions with reason codes, source_families) in the aggregate extraction payload of GET /documents/{id}, and surface the per-field decision + reason code in the review queue candidate cards and a quality-outcome chip on the document header, replacing the static 'Extraction pending' chip.

verdict.reasoning: Every factual claim reproduces against the working tree. claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py:58-62 writes claim_resolution_decisions and quality_outcome into aggregate metadata, which is persisted inside the aggregate extraction's normalized_json (reconciliation_repository.py:101-119) with row metadata_json holding only semanticAnnotationId (line 134). The document-detail SQL for document/aggregate-scope extractions (read_model.py:92-114) selects neither normalized_json nor metadata_json, and _extraction_payload (read_model.py:309-322) omits both — so the aggregate's outcome/decisions are unreachable via the detail API even though semantic-region rows (which never carry quality_outcome) do expose metadata. routes_review.py:24-67 exposes only review-tasks/field-candidates/canonical-fields; greps across apps/api and apps/web for quality_outcome, qualityOutcome, reason_code, claim_resolution_decisions, and the full outcome vocabulary (extracted_cleanly/needs_human_review/insufficient_signal/no_extraction_target) return zero hits, and no route exposes normalized_json at all. Review tasks carry only generic prose reasons ("Extraction requires review.", "{field_path} requires review." — canonical_repository.py:92,104), and the machine-readable reason codes (required_claim_absent, cross_field_arithmetic_conflict, cross_field_currency_conflict, line_item_sum_conflict, cross_field_plausibility_conflict) exist only in claim_resolver/claim_invariants/claim_registry/claim_decisions and the unexposed aggregate metadata. analysis_quality.py reads quality_outcome but its only consumer is analysis_intake.py (Phase 9 seam), which nothing in apps/ imports. The ADR 0005 Implementation Progress log records persistence of decisions and quality outcomes (2026-06-05 entries) but contains no entry claiming API/UI exposure, so the log does not refute the finding. Severity high is defensible for the spec-and-ui dimension: D8 makes outcomes first-class and D6's reason-code vocabulary exists to explain review demotions, yet the review UI can show only generic strings; the only mild mitigant is that D8's literal text requires persistence (satisfied), making this a missing consumption surface rather than a persistence-spec violation.

confirmed.title: Review queue 'Re-run extraction' enqueues a document-level Granite job that the live pipeline fails closed by design
confirmed.detail: ReviewService._enqueue_rerun creates a job_type='extract' payload with only target_schema_name (default 'receipt' via _target_schema_from_action) and no semantic_region_id. ExtractionService._semantic_task_for_document returns None when semantic_region_id is None, and ModelRoutingExtractionGateway raises ModelProtocolError for any structured schema (receipt/invoice/medical_eob are STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS, and the default route_profile 'docling_plus_structured_extraction' is a GRANITE_ROUTE_PROFILE) without a grounded semantic task — per the 2026-06-06 ADR entries that disabled broad document-level Granite extraction. So in live mode every review-queue re-run fails as a runtime/protocol error (eventually dead-lettered as pipeline_failed) instead of re-running anything. Compounding it, the web client's schemaFromReviewTask maps every non invoice/medical_eob/receipt field path — including observations.* and line_items.* tasks for service-record/retail-order/title documents — to targetSchemaName 'receipt', a schema those documents are explicitly barred from at candidate admission. The action is effectively guaranteed to fail or request the wrong schema.
confirmed.evidence: routing.py:51-55: 'if semantic_task is None: raise ModelProtocolError("Live Granite extraction requires a grounded semantic region task. Broad document-level structured extraction is disabled.")'; review/service.py builds payload via build_extract_document_job_payload with no semantic_region_id; reviewActions.ts:66: 'return "receipt";' as the fallthrough.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Change the rerun action to re-enqueue the Smart Parse path (semantic_annotate job, which re-plans regions and fans out Granite) or, for region-scoped tasks, re-enqueue the originating semantic-region extraction with its semantic_region_id; remove the 'receipt' default and derive the target from the task's extraction record. Disable or relabel the button for task types where re-extraction is meaningless.

verdict.reasoning:
Every step of the claimed failure chain reproduces in the current working tree, and the ADR 0005 Implementation Progress log contains no entry fixing the review re-run path.

Chain verified end-to-end:
1. UI: apps/web/src/components/ReviewQueue.tsx:173-190 `handleRerunExtraction` posts actionType "rerun_extraction" with metadata.targetSchemaName from `schemaFromReviewTask`. apps/web/src/reviewActions.ts:56-67 maps only `invoice.`/`medical_eob.`/`receipt.` field-path prefixes and falls through to `return "receipt";` for everything else (observations.*, line_items.*, service_record/retail_order paths). 2. Gateway: lib/extraction/gateways/routing.py:47-55 — granite_requested is True both ways ("docling_plus_structured_extraction" in GRANITE_ROUTE_PROFILES line 17; "receipt" in STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS line 21), and semantic_task None raises ModelProtocolError ("Live Granite extraction requires a grounded semantic region task. confirmed.title: observation_review, line_item_review, and relationship_suggestion tasks are unactionable in the review queue: no candidates, no evidence, no matching actions
confirmed.detail: Phase 8.5 creates review tasks for line-item candidates (fieldPath 'line_items.{type}.{ordinal}') and observation candidates (fieldPath 'observations.{family}.{field}'), and ADR 0005 routes all service_record/retail_order/title/escrow/dispute output into review-only document_observation aggregates — making observation review the primary human workflow for those families. But the only candidate-listing API is /field-candidates, which queries the field_candidates table by exact field_path; observation candidates live in extraction_observations and line-item candidates in their own table, so the queue shows these tasks with zero candidate cards: no value, no evidence, nothing to accept. The task mapper also drops metadata_json keys (observationId, lineItemCandidateId), so the UI cannot even fetch the referenced rows. The decision panel still offers field-shaped actions: 'Correct field' would write a canonical field under the synthetic 'observations.family.field' path, and accept is impossible. relationship_suggestion tasks (no fieldPath) get the same field-correct/reject/rerun panel even though accept/reject-relationship actions exist in the API and relationshipsApi.ts — they are only reachable from the separate Relationship workspace. Net effect: for exactly the document families the deterministic pipeline marks review-only, the reviewer can only 'Mark reviewed' blind.
confirmed.evidence: extraction_repository.py:330-335 stores '"observationId": str(candidate["id"])' in task metadata; mappers.py:10-22 maps only pageNumber/fieldPath from metadata; read_repository.py:58-61 'FROM field_candidates WHERE document_id = %s AND (... field_path = %s)' — no observation/line-item source; routes_review.py has no observation or line-item endpoints; ReviewDecisionPanel renders correct/reject/rerun unconditionally for every taskType.

(1) extraction_repository.py:294-307/323-336 create line_item_review and observation_review tasks with synthetic fieldPaths ("line_items.{type}.{ordinal}", "observations.{family}.{field}") and store lineItemCandidateId/observationId in metadata_json. (3) The only candidate API is GET /documents/{id}/field-candidates (routes_review.py:35-52) backed by read_repository.py:56-68 which queries field_candidates by exact field_path; observation candidates live in extraction_observations (observation_repository.py:26) and line items in line_item_candidates (candidate_repository.py:77), so ReviewQueue.tsx:55-62 loads zero candidate cards for these tasks — no value, no evidence, no Accept (handleAccept requires a FieldCandidate). (4) ReviewDecisionPanel.tsx:49-141 renders Correct/Reject/Reclassify/Rerun unconditionally for all taskTypes; "Correct field" on an observation task flows through service.py:41-54 to upsert_human_canonical_field (action_repository.py:45-80) which writes canonical_fields at the synthetic path with no validation — contradicting ADR 0005's review-only stance for these families (ADR lines 177-180, 230-234 confirm service_record/retail_order and unregistered families like title/escrow/dispute reconcile into review-only document_observation, making observation review the primary human workflow there). The ADR Implementation Progress log (through 2026-06-06) contains no entry fixing review-queue actionability for these task types, so nothing refutes the finding. lowerSeverity.title: Aggregate runs still round-trip projected JSON through legacy non-Claim candidate parsing, and every aggregate header field candidate is structurally rejected
lowerSeverity.detail: D3 says no engine output is reconciled in the target schema, and the Deferred Work item is to retire remaining non-Claim compatibility paths. The aggregate persistence path still calls field/line_item/observation_candidates_from_extraction on the projected aggregate JSON (reconciliation_repository.py:136-154), re-parsing the target schema instead of using the already-resolved Claims. Worse, the combination is internally inconsistent: claim_resolver field projection stores only typed_value per container field (claim_resolver.py:55-57), dropping the Claim anchor/evidence, so legacy _candidate() finds owner.get("evidence") empty (normalization.py:497) and the admission boundary then rejects every aggregate header field candidate with rejected_missing_evidence/missing_concrete_evidence — including invoice_number and total_amount that originated from fully anchored Granite Claims. Verified empirically: an invoice aggregate built from anchored claims produced field candidates [seller.display_name, invoice_number, total_amount] all with evidence=[] and all rejected at admission; zero admitted. Net effect: the aggregate-level field candidate path is dead weight that only generates rejection-event noise (canonical truth depends entirely on the separate region-level claim candidates), and provenance for aggregate header values is unrecoverable from the aggregate payload.

lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Either attach selected-claim evidence to projected header fields (mirroring line items, claim_resolver.py:168-171) so aggregate candidates carry anchors, or stop generating field candidates from aggregate payloads entirely and rely on region-level claim candidates, removing the legacy round-trip for aggregate runs.

lowerSeverity.title: Invoice aggregate substitutes amount_paid for missing total
lowerSeverity.detail: reconcile_invoice_region_extractions fills totals.total from totals.amount_paid when no invoice.total_amount claim resolved: `if "total" not in totals and "amount_paid" in totals: totals["total"] = totals["amount_paid"]`. For partially paid invoices, amount_paid is not the invoice total, so the canonical aggregate presents a wrong total value. The resolver still records an `absent`/`required_claim_absent` decision for invoice.total_amount (so the outcome is needs_human_review), but the projected payload now carries a fabricated total whose provenance is a different canonical key, contradicting D7 (output projected from accepted Claims) and risking a reviewer accepting the substituted value. This deterministic substitution is not declared anywhere in the registry or decision metadata.
lowerSeverity.evidence: reconciliation.py:57-58: `if "total" not in totals and "amount_paid" in totals: totals["total"] = totals["amount_paid"]` — no accompanying metadata flag or decision reason marks the substitution.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Remove the substitution, or record it explicitly (e.g. metadata repair `total_substituted_from_amount_paid` plus a needs_review decision on invoice.total_amount) so the projected total is never silently sourced from a different canonical key.

lowerSeverity.title: Invoice seller in canonical aggregate is a non-Claim, non-anchored external value
lowerSeverity.detail: The canonical invoice aggregate's seller container is built from source.counterparty_display ({"display_name": ..., "party_type": "company"}) and injected via extra_containers — it is not a Claim, has no Docling anchor, and bypasses the typed/anchored gates of D3/D4 (ADR: "Granite never becomes canonical without an anchor and validation"). There is also no invoice.seller field projection or claim key in INVOICE_CLAIM_REGISTRY, so a Granite/Docling-extracted seller can never compete with the external value. The seller candidate produced from the aggregate is always rejected at admission (empty evidence), so the only place the unanchored seller value survives is the canonical aggregate JSON itself, where reviewers and downstream consumers read it as extracted truth. Note the ADR's example registry lists invoice.seller as a required key; the implementation neither claims it nor anchors it.

lowerSeverity.title: Structured-output retry classification duplicates exact adapter message strings in two modules
