lowerSeverity.title: Reconciliation is not exactly-once: unguarded check-then-act race can build the aggregate twice
lowerSeverity.detail: The trigger check (expected count vs completed rows) runs in its own connection/transaction with no lock, and the aggregate persist happens later in a second transaction. If the last two region jobs complete on concurrent extraction workers, both workers can observe len(rows) == expected_count and both run _reconcile_regions and persist_extraction_run for the same annotation. The document FOR UPDATE lock only serializes the persists; the second aggregate supersedes the first, but duplicate candidate rows, admission events, canonical history entries, and derived asset versions are written, and downstream embedding/relationship refreshes fire twice. With a single worker this is serial, but the worker design (claim_next_job_record polling) clearly anticipates horizontal scaling.
lowerSeverity.evidence: maybe_reconcile_semantic_annotation: 'with db_connection() as conn: ... _expected_region_job_count ... _current_region_extraction_rows' (read-only txn), followed much later by persist_extraction_run(...) in a separate connection; no advisory lock or idempotency key ties the aggregate to (annotation_id, region-row fingerprint).
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Take a pg advisory lock on (document_id, semantic_annotation_id, schema) around the check+persist, or perform the completeness check inside the persist transaction after locking the document, skipping if a current aggregate already covers the same region extraction set.

lowerSeverity.title: Docling worker swallows semantic-annotation enqueue failures; parsed documents silently never enter extraction
lowerSeverity.detail: After complete_job succeeds, the worker enqueues embeddings and the semantic_annotate job in separate try/except blocks that only call _record_downstream_enqueue_failure (a service-health 'degraded' snapshot which itself swallows errors). The docling job is already marked succeeded, so a transient DB failure during enqueue leaves the document parsed but with NO semantic annotation job, hence no Qwen planning, no Granite extraction, no claims, no review tasks — and no retryable job or review artifact to recover it. Only the operator CLI reprocess path can fix it, and the only signal is a transient health metric.
lowerSeverity.evidence: worker.py: 'try: _enqueue_semantic_annotation(...) except Exception as exc: downstream_failures.append(f"semantic:{exc.__class__.__name__}")' followed by _record_downstream_enqueue_failure which only calls record_service_health and prints on failure.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Enqueue the semantic-annotation job in the same transaction/commit as job completion (create_job_with_cursor alongside complete), or enqueue before complete_job so a failure keeps the docling job retryable.

lowerSeverity.title: Retail-order planning keeps only one line-item table region per page; second table on a page is silently dropped
lowerSeverity.detail: _retail_order_line_item_ids_to_keep selects a single best retail_order_line_item_table region per page_number (best_by_page keyed on page) and _normalize_retail_order_regions drops the rest. A retail order page with two genuine item tables (e.g., two shipments, or items + returns) loses the second table before planning; the dropped region never becomes a plan task (so unlike planner budget drops it is not even recorded as skipped), and the document_observation aggregate for retail orders omits those rows with no review/quality marker.
lowerSeverity.evidence: manifest_normalization.py: 'best_by_page: dict[int, ...]; ... if current is None or key < current[0]: best_by_page[page_number] = (key, region)' then 'if id(region) not in line_item_ids_to_keep: continue'.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Key the keep-set on (page_number, table_id) so distinct Docling tables on one page survive, or record the dropped regions as plan-task skips with a review marker.

lowerSeverity.title: Contract boundary fails open when the model-output schema cannot be loaded
lowerSeverity.detail: The (uncommitted) fail-closed whole-payload validation in contract_root_payload returns the payload unchanged with no rejected fields and no contract errors when model_output_schema_name is None OR load_model_output_schema raises KeyError/OSError/ValueError. A job carrying a schema name the running code no longer registers (e.g., contract renamed between enqueue and execution during a rolling deploy, or fixture/direct callers with stale names) is mined by mapper logic with zero contract enforcement — the opposite of the boundary's fail-closed intent, and silent (no lineage metadata records the skip).
lowerSeverity.evidence: contract_root_payload: 'try: schema = load_model_output_schema(model_output_schema_name).schema except (KeyError, OSError, ValueError): return payload, [], []'.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: When a non-None schema name fails to load, fail closed ({}, [], ['model_output_schema_unloadable: <name>']) so the extraction surfaces as a contract failure instead of unvalidated mining.

lowerSeverity.title: Invoice aggregate fabricates totals.total from amount_paid without marking it derived
lowerSeverity.detail: reconcile_invoice_region_extractions sets totals['total'] = totals['amount_paid'] whenever no total claim was resolved. For partially paid invoices this asserts a wrong canonical total in the aggregate payload (and the synthesized value is then mined into an invoice total field candidate by reconciliation_repository's candidate pass) with no decision/reason-code marking it as derived rather than claimed, contrary to D6's per-key decision+provenance model. The arithmetic invariant cannot catch it because there is no independent total claim to conflict with.
lowerSeverity.evidence: reconciliation.py: 'if "total" not in totals and "amount_paid" in totals: totals["total"] = totals["amount_paid"]' — unconditional copy with no metadata/decision annotation.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Either drop the substitution (leave totals.total absent with the existing required_claim_absent decision) or record an explicit derived-value decision/reason code and force the field to needs_review.

lowerSeverity.title: Aggregate field candidates lose claim anchors/evidence at the projection seam
lowerSeverity.detail: The resolver stores only selected.typed_value into projection.fields (no evidence/anchor), project_claim_family_payload projects those bare values into aggregate containers, and reconciliation_repository then mines field candidates from the aggregate JSON via the legacy field_candidates_from_extraction path with source_engine='system' (which bypasses the model concrete-anchor requirement). Resulting aggregate field candidates carry no claim anchor, so review-UI evidence jumps and the concrete-evidence promotion gate for these document-level facts lose the provenance the Claim IR was built to preserve (line items keep their evidence; only container fields drop it). Selected claim ids survive only inside metadata.claim_resolution_decisions, which the candidate path does not read.
lowerSeverity.evidence: claim_resolver.py: 'fields.setdefault(field_projection.container, {})[field_projection.field_name] = selected.typed_value'; reconciliation_repository.py: 'field_candidates_from_extraction(document_id=..., schema_name=aggregate_schema_name, payload=aggregate_json, ..., source_engine=gateway_extraction.route.source_engine)' where source_engine='system'.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Build aggregate field candidates directly from the selected Claims (field_candidates_from_claims) instead of re-mining the projected payload, or project per-field evidence alongside typed values.

lowerSeverity.title: Dead code: stale Granite prompt builder and unused invoice line-item renumber helper
lowerSeverity.detail: _vision.py's module-level _prompt() is unused (the gateway uses granite_prompting.granite_prompt) and instructs the model to return the legacy '{"normalized": {...}, "confidence": {...}}' wrapper shape that the ADR explicitly removed (the adapter no longer unwraps 'normalized' wrappers and would fail such payloads). If ever re-wired it would systematically produce schema-invalid output. reconciliation.py _renumber() is also unreferenced.
lowerSeverity.evidence: _vision.py:389-391: 'Return JSON only in this shape: {"normalized":{...target schema JSON...},"confidence":{...}}' vs ADR 2026-06-06: 'The vision adapter no longer unwraps a schema-valid {"normalized": ..., "confidence": ...} wrapper'; grep shows no callers of either function.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Delete both helpers.

lowerSeverity.title: Arithmetic invariants treat missing optional components as 0 and use exact equality, demoting correct totals to needs_review
lowerSeverity.detail: (1) Optional addends/subtrahends (tax_total, shipping_total, tip, discount_total) that have no selected claim are summed as 0, so any invoice/receipt where the document has tax but Granite did not emit a tax claim gets its correct total demoted with cross_field_arithmetic_conflict. The invariant cannot distinguish 'component absent from extraction' from 'component is zero', producing a systematic false-positive review load on partially-extracted documents (extraction of tax fields is exactly what fails most often). (2) `if target_amount == expected: continue` is exact Decimal equality with no tolerance, while MONEY_TOLERANCE (0.02) is defined in the same module and used by the upper-bound invariant and by validators._money_match; one-cent printed rounding differences (per-line tax rounding) demote legitimate totals. Both effects are fail-safe (review, not corruption) but inflate needs_human_review and dilute reviewer trust in reason codes.
lowerSeverity.evidence: Reproduced: claims [invoice.subtotal=100.00, invoice.total_amount=108.25] (no tax claim) -> decision 'invoice.total_amount needs_review cross_field_arithmetic_conflict', quality needs_human_review, even though the document's total is correct and tax was simply not extracted. claim_invariants.py:116 `if target_amount == expected: continue` (no MONEY_TOLERANCE); lines 102-114 sum optional amounts with missing -> 0.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Skip the arithmetic invariant (or use a distinct reason code like arithmetic_unverifiable_missing_components) when any optional component referenced by the document family is unresolved; compare with abs(target-expected) <= MONEY_TOLERANCE.

lowerSeverity.title: Typed date claims are never normalized to ISO; MM/DD/YYYY values poison format:"date" canonical contracts and verbose dates are dropped
lowerSeverity.detail: _typed_value('date', ...) accepts "%Y-%m-%d", "%m/%d/%Y", "%m/%d/%y" but returns the raw string unchanged. Projection writes it verbatim into invoice.issued_on / transaction.date_local, which $ref localDate with format:"date", and ContractRegistry validates with Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER -- so a Granite date "03/04/2025" makes the entire aggregate fail JSON-schema validation (json_schema failed -> needs_review, family checks skipped). It also destabilizes identity: the same date as "2025-03-04" vs "03/04/2025" yields different claim_ids and different canonical-output fingerprints across runs if the model alternates formats. Meanwhile "March 4, 2025" fails _is_date_like and the claim is dropped entirely, even though candidate_value_parsing.date_value (used on the candidate path) parses it -- the two date parsers disagree about what is a date.
lowerSeverity.evidence: Verified: _typed_value('date','03/04/2025') -> ('date','03/04/2025'); _typed_value('date','3/4/25') -> ('date','3/4/25'); _typed_value('date','March 4, 2025') -> None. common_defs.schema.json localDate: {type: string, format: date}; lib/contracts/registry.py:117 passes format_checker=Draft202012Validator.FORMAT_CHECKER.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Normalize typed dates to ISO-8601 in _typed_value (strptime then .date().isoformat()), and use the same deterministic parser (date_value) for both the claim typer and the candidate path; keep the original string in raw_value.

lowerSeverity.title: Contract boundary fails open when the contract cannot be loaded, has no root properties, or is itself invalid
lowerSeverity.detail: contract_root_payload returns (payload, [], []) -- i.e. accepts the whole payload unvalidated -- when load_model_output_schema raises (KeyError/OSError/ValueError: missing file, renamed contract, stale schema name from a replayed DB row), when schema['properties'] is not a dict, and when Draft202012Validator.check_schema raises SchemaError. For a model_output_schema_name that matches no mapper branch, normalize_granite_region_output then returns the raw model payload as 'normalized' output (line 192-195) with zero contract enforcement. The uncommitted change is otherwise a correct tightening (whole-payload fail-closed instead of pruning/completion), but these three escape hatches contradict the fail-closed design for the direct/fixture/replay path the change is meant to close. ADR D2/D4 and the 2026-06-06 log entries describe the boundary as fail-closed.
lowerSeverity.evidence: Demonstrated: contract_root_payload({'anything':'goes','invoice_number':'INV-9','totals':{'junk':1}}, model_output_schema_name='granite_invoice_line_items.v9') -> fail-open passthrough: True, rejected: [], errors: []. Code: `except (KeyError, OSError, ValueError): return payload, [], []` (line 20-21) and `except SchemaError: return []` (line 97-98).
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: When model_output_schema_name is non-None and the schema cannot be loaded or is unusable, return ({}, [], [f'contract_unavailable:{name}']) so the payload fails closed with explicit lineage, mirroring the validation-failure path.

lowerSeverity.title: Receipt family has no aggregate reconciliation path despite registry aggregate metadata
lowerSeverity.detail: AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"} and _reconcile_regions has no receipt branch, so maybe_reconcile_semantic_annotation returns None for schema_name="receipt". Receipt is a first-class family whose registry declares aggregate_schema_name="receipt", aggregate_line_items_key, required containers, and receipt-specific invariants -- but no canonical receipt.v1 aggregate is ever assembled from receipt regions. Concretely: a receipt document yields a line-items region (granite_receipt_line_items.v1) and a payment-summary region (granite_receipt_payment_summary.v1); merchant/date/tip/discount from one region and line items from the other are never co-resolved, so the cross-region receipt total arithmetic and required-key (receipt.transaction.total) gates only ever run per-region, and no document-level canonical receipt payload exists, unlike invoice and medical_eob.
lowerSeverity.evidence: reconciliation_repository.py:36 `AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {"invoice", "medical_eob", "document_observation"}`; _reconcile_regions (lines 166-198) returns None for receipt; claim_registry.py:193 `aggregate_schema_name="receipt"` is referenced nowhere by an aggregate wrapper (grep for receipt aggregate reconcilers returns only the registry line).
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Add a receipt branch using the shared resolve_claim_regions_for_family + project_claim_family_payload path (the registry data already exists), or remove the receipt aggregate metadata from the registry if intentionally deferred and document it in the ADR Deferred Work.

lowerSeverity.title: Agreement detection compares full typed_value JSON, so currency-presence differences and same-engine duplicates mislabel decisions
lowerSeverity.detail: _resolve_key computes unique_values over the full typed_value JSON. Two claims asserting the same amount where one carries an explicit currency and the other does not (e.g. {'amount':50.0,'currency':'USD'} vs {'amount':50.0}, which arises via region_envelope._line_item_payload reconstructing money without currency_code) are classified as source_precedence_conflict -> needs_review, dropping the agreement boost the spec promises ('>=2 sources agreeing => high confidence'). Conversely, two claims from the same engine with equal values are labeled multi_source_agreement even though only one source corroborated the value. Behavior is deterministic and fail-safe, but the reason codes drive quality outcome and review payloads, so agreement boosting is lost and review reasons are misleading.
lowerSeverity.evidence: Reproduced: two granite invoice.total_amount claims with typed values {'amount':50.0,'currency':'USD'} and {'amount':50.0} -> decision 'needs_review source_precedence_conflict'. Code: claim_resolver.py:186 `unique_values = {_stable_value_key(claim.typed_value) for claim in ordered}` and 187-193 reason selection never inspects claim.source_engine.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Compare money agreement on amount (and on currency only when both are explicit), and require len({claim.source_engine}) >= 2 for the multi_source_agreement reason; use e.g. single_source_corroborated for same-engine duplicates.

lowerSeverity.title: Medical EOB line-item candidates silently drop allowed_amount and plan_paid; sparse rows with only unlisted money fields are discarded
lowerSeverity.detail: The ADR log (2026-06-05) states allowed/plan-paid amounts are preserved 'into medical_eob.v1 line-item projection instead of dropping them before reconciliation' -- the aggregate projection does preserve them, but the candidate path does not: the medical_eob branch of _line_item_candidate_from_projection maps only procedure_code/units/billed_amount/patient_responsibility, and LineItemCandidateFact has no allowed_amount/plan_paid fields, so persisted service-line candidates (and their fingerprints/dedupe keys) lose the payer-side amounts. Separately, _line_item_has_value's hard-coded key list omits family-mapped field names (receipt 'sku'/'discount', service_record 'line_total', EOB 'allowed_amount'/'plan_paid'), so e.g. a service-record row whose only resolved values are line_total and unit is dropped from the projection entirely despite holding an anchored money claim.
lowerSeverity.evidence: claim_candidates.py:198-214 constructs the EOB LineItemCandidateFact without item.get('allowed_amount')/item.get('plan_paid') even though _resolve_line_items emits those keys (claim_registry.py:266-267 maps allowed_amount/plan_paid). claim_resolver.py:333-347 key list: description, code, quantity, unit_price, gross_amount, tax_amount, amount, service_description, procedure_code, units, billed_amount, patient_responsibility -- no line_total/sku/discount/allowed_amount/plan_paid.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Derive _line_item_has_value's value-bearing keys from the family registry field_map values instead of a hard-coded list; extend LineItemCandidateFact (or its metadata) with allowed/plan-paid amounts.

lowerSeverity.title: Fabricated gross_amount claims (gross := net) for invoice/service-record line items
lowerSeverity.detail: region_envelope._line_item sets gross_amount=_money_amount(item.get('billed_amount') or item.get('amount')). Invoice/receipt/service-record normalized items have no billed_amount, so gross_amount is silently set equal to the net amount, and claims.py then emits a separate invoice.line_item.gross_amount Claim (registry admits it) whose value the model never asserted. claim_candidates doubles down with `gross_amount = item.get('gross_amount') or amount`. Canonical invoice line items therefore always report gross == net even when the document distinguishes them, and the duplicated money claim inflates claim counts/fingerprints. (Receipt is unaffected only because its registry field_map omits gross_amount, so the claim is dropped at admission.)
lowerSeverity.evidence: region_envelope.py:482 `gross_amount=_money_amount(item.get("billed_amount") or item.get("amount"))`; e2e repro produced 9 claims for 3 receipt items (3 per row: description, quantity, amount) but an invoice payload produces an extra gross_amount claim per row mirroring amount.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Set gross_amount only from an explicit billed/gross source key per schema family; leave it None otherwise.

lowerSeverity.title: Dead code: _renumber() unused; invoice.seller.display_name facts are emitted but always inadmissible
lowerSeverity.detail: _renumber in reconciliation.py is defined but never called (ordinals are assigned in claim_projection._projected_line_items). region_envelope._facts_from_projection emits 'invoice.seller.display_name' facts (line 260), but the invoice family registry has no such field projection and the key does not match the line-item prefix, so claim_key_is_admissible returns False and the fact is unconditionally dropped at claims._claim_from_fact -- seller evidence extracted by Granite never becomes a Claim and the invoice wrapper relies solely on external source.counterparty_display. Either register the key or stop emitting the fact; as-is it is silent dead weight that looks like working seller extraction.
lowerSeverity.evidence: grep '_renumber' shows only the definition at reconciliation.py:159. claim_registry.py invoice field_projections (lines 67-80) contain no invoice.seller.* key; claims.py:156-157 `if not claim_key_is_admissible(fact.name): return None` drops it.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Delete _renumber; either add ClaimFieldProjection('invoice.seller.display_name', 'seller', 'display_name', ('party','text')) or remove the seller fact emission.

lowerSeverity.title: PARTIALLY FIXED: Granite instruction/schema echo — constrained decoding is strict and fail-closed, but content echo passes shape validation and the canonical aggregate path bypasses the echo gates
lowerSeverity.detail: Implemented and verified: the adapter always sends strict json_schema and re-validates the returned object against the exact requested schema (_openai_vision.py:219-230, ModelProtocolError on mismatch); the live Granite request always carries response_json_schema (_vision.py:345-347); item-level admission only accepts contract-declared keys; whole-payload fail-closed contract validation is in the working tree (model_output_contract_boundary.py:26-29). Residual gaps: (1) constrained decoding only constrains SHAPE — instruction/schema echo inside free-text fields (description, category_hint) is schema-valid; (2) the content gate is still a small, corpus-specific deny-list (PROMPT_ECHO_PATTERNS includes literal observed typos like 'extruct the schema', 'tabls schema'), exactly the unbounded reject-list ADR D4 was supposed to retire; (3) D4's premise 'artifacts have no anchor' does not hold because line-item anchors are synthesized from the region's grounding context (line_item_provenance/evidence_ref_from_context attach table_id/page/bbox regardless of content), so echo rows pass the anchor and typing gates and become Claims; (4) the claim resolver and invoice/EOB aggregate projection apply NO echo gate (reject_line_item is only applied in claim_candidates.py:190 and candidate_admission.py:315), so an echo row can appear in canonical aggregate line_items even while its candidate is rejected at admission. For receipts specifically there is no document-level aggregate (AGGREGATE_RECONCILIATION_SCHEMAS = {invoice, medical_eob, document_observation}), so receipt line items do flow through the echo-gated candidate path — the receipt-specific exposure is materially reduced, but invoice/EOB canonical aggregates retain the bypass.
lowerSeverity.evidence: _openai_vision.py:219-230: Draft202012Validator(response_schema).validate(parsed) ... 'Vision model JSON content does not match response schema.'; candidate_quality_policy.py PROMPT_ECHO_PATTERNS = ("identify and extract", "extract the schema", "extruct the schema", "tabls schema", ...); claim_resolver._resolve_line_items has no content gate; reconciliation.py:62-72 projects claim_projection.line_items into the canonical invoice payload with only _dedupe_line_item_dicts applied; line_item_provenance.py:36-45 builds evidence from evidence_context for every model row.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Apply reject_line_item (or a Claim-level content gate) inside _resolve_line_items or before aggregate projection so canonical aggregates and admitted candidates share one echo policy; longer term, verify row content against the anchored Docling cell text instead of growing the phrase deny-list.

lowerSeverity.title: PARTIALLY FIXED: Low-signal table-cell junk filtering exists only at the candidate layer; document_observation aggregates project claims with no signal gate and the grid filter covers only 'cells'/'dimensions'
lowerSeverity.detail: Progress since the corpus run: normalization drops schema/meta keys, empties, and echo phrases (should_drop_observation, model_output_observations.py:164-186); contract-derived key allow-lists bound generic KVP and direct-field observation shapes; and the candidate path applies reject_observation + empty_observation_value + grid_only_observation (claim_candidates.py:249-252). Remaining gaps: grid_only_observation only triggers for field names exactly 'dimensions' or 'cells' (candidate_value_parsing.py:99-105), so other low-signal cell fragments (single-token header cells, bare numbers with generic names from granite_generic_kvp.v1, repeated column labels) pass; and the document_observation AGGREGATE path (observation_reconciliation -> claim_resolver._resolve_document_observations -> project_document_observation_payload) projects observations straight from anchored Claims with no junk/signal filter at all — reject_observation and grid_only_observation are never invoked on that path, so junk that the candidate layer would reject still lands in the canonical document_observation.v1 payload that review reads.
lowerSeverity.evidence: candidate_value_parsing.py:99-105: 'if field == "dimensions": return True / if field != "cells": return False'; claim_resolver.py:94-127 _resolve_document_observations builds observations from grouped claims with only _resolve_key selection; claim_projection.py:56-68 projects projection.observations into the payload unfiltered; grep for reject_observation/grid_only across claim_resolver.py, claim_projection.py, observation_reconciliation.py returns nothing.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Apply the same observation quality gate (reject_observation + empty_observation_value + grid_only_observation, plus a minimal signal score for single-token/numeric-fragment values from generic KVP) inside _resolve_document_observations or project_document_observation_payload so candidate and aggregate layers share one policy.

lowerSeverity.title: FIXED: Semantic/document-family supersede/downgrade now writes the same documents.document_family read model the API/UI/search read
lowerSeverity.detail: Verified end-to-end in the working tree: apply_semantic_document_family_decision_with_cursor updates documents.document_family/document_subtype/family_confidence (with the medical sensitivity rule) for every family in PERSISTABLE_DOCUMENT_FAMILIES, all of which exist in document_family_enum after migration 081. The Phase 4 classifier no longer clobbers a semantic decision — _update_document_classification guards every column behind 'WHEN metadata_json #> {phase8_5,semantic_classification} IS NOT NULL THEN <keep>'. Reads are coherent: document detail (read_model.py:241), document lists (list_repository.py:28), search results, facets, and family filters (search/repository.py:104,153,424) all read d.document_family directly; the web UI family enumerations include the new families (retail_order, service_record, mortgage_escrow_statement, etc. in SearchFilterPanel.tsx and ReviewDecisionPanel.tsx). document_chunks.document_family_snapshot is refreshed from d.document_family on every extraction persistence (extraction_repository.py:263-264), so the snapshot staleness window is bounded to the moments between the semantic-family update and the first region extraction. No remaining read-model mismatch found.
lowerSeverity.evidence: extraction_repository.py:386-389: 'SET document_family = CASE WHEN metadata_json #> '{phase8_5,semantic_classification}' IS NOT NULL THEN document_family ELSE %s::document_family_enum END'; semantic_family.py:223-251 updates documents directly; search/repository.py:424 'd.document_family::text = ANY(%s::text[])'.

lowerSeverity.title: PARTIALLY FIXED: Confidence is now excluded from deterministic decisions, but end-to-end it remains uncalibrated model self-report mixed with hard-coded constants, and the 0.78 auto-promotion gate consumes it directly
lowerSeverity.detail: What confidence means now, stage by stage: Granite self-reports a region-level confidence dict (contract-required, nullable) and optional per-field confidences; these pass through normalization, envelope, Claim (claim.confidence), and candidate (claim_candidates.py:170) untouched. The resolver correctly no longer uses confidence for precedence or tie-breaks (_claim_sort_key is source-authority + stable value + claim_id), and repeatability fingerprints exclude it — the stochasticity fix from the ADR log is real. But coherence is not achieved: (1) auto-promotion gates on the raw self-reported value (canonical_repository.py:32: '(candidate["confidence"] or 0) < 0.78'), i.e., an uncalibrated model self-assessment decides canonical promotion; (2) synthesized constants masquerade as confidence — evidence refs default to 0.72 (evidence_concretizer.py:76, line_item_provenance.py:42), indistinguishable from a genuine 0.72; (3) the invoice line-items contract has no per-item confidence at all, so line-item claims carry None; (4) the spec's '>=2 sources agreeing => high confidence' is implemented only as a reason_code (multi_source_agreement) — no confidence value is ever raised, and resolver-projected fields/line items drop confidence entirely, while aggregate payload 'confidence' is just the region coverage dict; (5) Qwen page/region confidences are averaged into 'overall' and repair paths clamp to 0.2 (_low_confidence), while semantic-family confidence is a heuristic constant family (0.72+0.04*anchors capped 0.96 / 0.68 / 0.62) persisted to documents.family_confidence. So a single 'confidence' field spans at least four unrelated semantics across the pipeline.
lowerSeverity.evidence: claim_resolver.py:222-227 _claim_sort_key = (-SOURCE_PRECEDENCE.get(source_engine,0), _stable_value_key(typed_value), claim_id) — no confidence; canonical_repository.py:32 'if candidate["status"] != "proposed" or (candidate["confidence"] or 0) < 0.78: continue'; evidence_concretizer.py:75-76 'else: evidence["confidence"] = 0.72'; granite_invoice_line_items.v1 item required keys contain no 'confidence'; _resolve_key emits reason codes only, never adjusts confidence.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Define a deterministic derived-confidence policy at the resolver (e.g., map multi_source_agreement/single_source/conflict + anchor specificity to bands), use that for promotion instead of raw self-report, and tag synthesized defaults (0.72) as 'confidence_source: default' so they can never satisfy promotion or review thresholds.

lowerSeverity.title: OPEN: No expected-field vs actual-output telemetry — the system cannot tell when Granite returned fewer fields than the plan expected
lowerSeverity.detail: The plan's expected_fields are produced by Qwen, persisted on the semantic task, written into job payloads (semantic_expected_fields, event_payloads.py:64-65), and embedded into Granite prompts (granite_prompting.py:34). Their ONLY downstream consumption is the crop-retry usefulness heuristic (visual_input_planning.py:159: observations non-empty when the task has expected_fields). Nothing compares expected_fields against the fields/claims Granite actually returned: repo-wide grep for field_coverage / fields_returned / missing_expected / expected_vs returns nothing; validators.py has only arithmetic/date checks; quality_outcomes derive solely from resolver decisions (registry required_keys), which cover registry-required canonical keys, not the per-region plan expectation. So a region planned for ['vin','mileage','repair_order_number'] that returns one field persists as a normal extraction with no coverage signal, no review reason, and no metric — the exact blind spot the May review flagged. The required_claim_absent decisions added 2026-06-05 partially cover REGISTRY-required keys at the family level, but per-region plan expectation coverage remains unmeasured.
lowerSeverity.evidence: Only three consumers of expected_fields outside semantic planning: granite_prompting.py:34 (prompt text), visual_input_planning.py:159 (retry usefulness), event_payloads.py:64-65 (payload write, never read back by workers/extraction). No comparison code exists in lib/, workers/, or scripts/.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: At envelope/claim construction, record expected_field_coverage = {expected, returned, missing} in normalization metadata, surface it in candidateAdmissionSummary/quality telemetry, and optionally demote quality_outcome to needs_human_review when coverage for a high-priority region falls below a threshold.

lowerSeverity.title: PARTIALLY FIXED: Cross-window continuation reconciliation — claims pooling merges multi-page tables generically, but continuation_group is never used at reconciliation time and line-item ordering breaks lexicographically at indices >= 10
lowerSeverity.detail: What works: aggregate assembly pools claims from ALL current same-family regions (claim_aggregate_reconciliation.py:30-52), so multi-page line-item tables do combine into one canonical aggregate without continuation-specific code; continuation_group correctly forces per-page full-page visual plans (visual_input_planning.py:642 'continuation_requires_per_page_visual_plan') and feeds Docling table-quality continuation risk (_vision.py:480). What is missing: continuation_group never reaches reconciliation — no module under lib/extraction/ references it — so there is no stitching/completeness check (a missing continuation segment silently shrinks the table with no signal), no cross-page repeated-header or carried-subtotal handling, and cross-window semantic-type drift on the same table produces duplicates (see finding 1). Additionally, the ADR log claim that rows 'project in physical row order' (2026-06-06 entry) is contradicted by the code: _resolve_line_items orders groups by _stable_value_key(anchor.as_json()), a lexicographic JSON-string sort, so row_index 10 sorts before row_index 2 and page_number 10 before page 2 (verified by repro: json key '{"...row_index":10...' < '...row_index":2...'). Long tables (>=10 rows) and documents with >=10 pages project line items out of physical order — deterministic, but wrong order for review/UI and for any order-sensitive consumer.
lowerSeverity.evidence: claim_resolver.py:144 'anchor_key = _stable_value_key(claim.anchor.as_json())' with :252-255 _stable_value_key = json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True); repro confirms sorted([row10_key, row2_key])[0] == row10_key. grep 'continuation' across lib/extraction reconciliation modules returns nothing; ADR line 493-496 claims 'project in physical row order'.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Sort line-item groups by a numeric tuple (page_number, table_id, row_index, ordinal) instead of the anchor JSON string; add a continuation-group completeness check in aggregate metadata (expected continuation segments vs regions present) so missing segments demote to needs_human_review.

lowerSeverity.title: OPEN: No proactive Qwen input-budget estimation/warning before live dispatch — token-budget telemetry exists only in the canary harness
lowerSeverity.detail: Exactly as cerebrum records ('the live production path still benefits from proactive input-budget warnings before dispatch if context pressure returns'): the canary harness computes a full token-budget report (visual-token estimates from rendered image dimensions, Docling context/prompt/schema token estimates, requested output tokens, conservative per-window totals — run_phase8_5_semantic_canary.py:596-735), but the live QwenSemanticAnnotationGateway builds the prompt, Docling context, and full-size page-image fan-in and dispatches with zero input-size estimation, no warning log, and no pre-dispatch telemetry (_generate_for_source, _image_inputs). There is also no context-length error classification anywhere in lib/model_runtime (no 'context_length'/'maximum context' handling), and retry_policy treats context overflows as non-retryable generic failures, so when context pressure returns (longer documents, larger Docling outlines, 4-image windows) the first signal will be opaque pipeline_failed jobs rather than a budget warning. Given documents up to max_images pages per window and a 6144-token output budget (SMART_SEMANTIC_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), this is a production-readiness observability gap rather than a correctness bug.
lowerSeverity.evidence: qwen_gateway.py:229-241 VisionGenerateRequest(... prompt=_prompt(...), image_inputs=_image_inputs(...), max_output_tokens=..., temperature=0.0 ...) with no estimation calls; grep for context_length/max_model_len/token_budget across lib/semantic_annotations and lib/model_runtime returns nothing; canary-only _token_budget_report at scripts/gpu/run_phase8_5_semantic_canary.py:596.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Extract the canary's _token_budget_report estimators into a shared lib module, compute a conservative per-window estimate in _generate_for_source before dispatch, log/persist it as manifest telemetry, and emit an explicit warning (or proactively shrink the window) when the estimate approaches the profile's context limit.

lowerSeverity.title: OPEN: Intent fields (requested_by, requested_by_user_id, user_intent_reason) flow through job payloads into ExtractionService and are silently discarded — never persisted on extraction runs
lowerSeverity.detail: Still true in the working tree. build_extract_document_job_payload writes requested_by_user_id and user_intent_reason into the job payload (event_payloads.py:76-77), the extraction worker reads them back and passes them into ExtractionService.extract_document (worker.py:121-127), and extract_document declares all three parameters (service.py:146-148) — but the method body never references any of them: they are not added to the semantic task run_metadata lineage (service.py:161-169 only carries plan/contract fields), and persist_extraction_run has no intent parameters (extraction_repository.py:68-79), so nothing reaches extraction rows, normalization metadata, or audit. The only durable copy is the raw job payload JSON; once jobs are pruned/archived, who/why an extraction ran is unrecoverable from extraction lineage. For a review-centric system this loses provenance the API surface clearly intended to keep (the parameters were threaded through three layers).
lowerSeverity.evidence: grep -n 'requested_by|user_intent_reason' lib/extraction/service.py returns only lines 118 (classifier literal 'system'), 146, 147, 148 — declarations with zero body usage; persist_extraction_run signature (extraction_repository.py:68-79) has no intent fields.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Either persist them (add to the run lineage metadata passed through _semantic_task_for_document or as columns/metadata in _insert_extraction_run_row) or remove the dead parameters from extract_document and the worker call to stop implying they are recorded.

lowerSeverity.title: OPEN: Routing gateway STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS still omits document_observation — latent silent fallback to the deterministic gateway for non-Granite route profiles
lowerSeverity.detail: The June finding is literally still true: routing.py:21 STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS = {"receipt", "invoice", "medical_eob"} while TARGET_EXTRACTION_SCHEMAS (classification.py:10) includes document_observation. The gap bites only for a document_observation extraction carrying a route_profile outside GRANITE_ROUTE_PROFILES (a malformed/legacy payload, or any future caller): instead of failing closed or routing to Granite like the other three target schemas would, it silently falls through to DoclingHeuristicGateway, producing deterministic-heuristic output labeled as a normal extraction. lowerSeverity.title: Model health probes are not persisted, omit the probed service URL, and cannot distinguish a placeholder or wrong model from the real service
lowerSeverity.detail: Three related gaps in the health/SLO surface. (1) The June finding is unfixed: _probe_snapshot records only `error_class` in metrics_json — neither the probed URL nor any endpoint identity — so an 'unavailable' row cannot be triaged to a wrong STRUCTURA_MODEL_*_URL without container inspection. (2) Probe results are computed inline per admin request and never written to service_health_snapshots (record_service_health is only called by worker heartbeats), so there is no model-service health history, trend, or SLO window; the queue metrics that are attached are lifetime counts (no time window) using an `error_json::text ILIKE '%timeout%'` heuristic. (3) Status 'ok' only requires /healthz|/health < 300. The placeholder model services (compose profile ["models-placeholder", "models"] — note plain "models" maps to placeholders) serve exactly that endpoint on the live Granite/embed ports 8101-8103, and a vLLM serving the wrong model also passes. The probe never checks /v1/models served-model name against profile.base_model, so health can report 'ok' while every extraction request 404s.
lowerSeverity.evidence: health.py:166-168: `except Exception as exc: status = "unavailable"; metrics["error_class"] = exc.__class__.__name__` — no url field anywhere in _base_metrics (184-201). routes_admin.py:36-42 recomputes snapshots per request and only merges them into the response; no INSERT. compose.yaml:341/356/371: placeholders carry profile "models"; workers/model_placeholder.py serves only /healthz returning {"status": "ok"}.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Add `url` (and optionally `base_model`) to probe metrics; verify served model identity via GET /v1/models for vLLM-backed services; persist probe snapshots via record_service_health on a worker heartbeat or scheduled probe so the admin surface has history; rename the placeholder compose profile so plain `models` is not a placeholder alias.

lowerSeverity.title: Job-layer failure policy ignores exception retryability: deterministic failures retry 5x, while Granite timeouts on one route dead-letter immediately
lowerSeverity.detail: ModelRuntimeError defines a per-class `retryable` contract (ModelTimeoutError/ModelServiceError True, ModelConfigurationError/ModelProtocolError False) but no worker consults it — the only consumer of any retry policy is extraction_failure_policy, which special-cases exactly one combination (ModelTimeoutError + route 'docling_plus_granite_structured' → non-retryable) and returns retryable=True for everything else. Consequences: (a) deterministic failures (ModelConfigurationError from a bad URL, ModelProtocolError after the adapter has already retried once per ADR D2, UUID parse errors, 'Unsupported extraction queue job') burn 5 job attempts — and for Granite structured-output failures each attempt doubles model calls via the adapter-level retry, ~10 GPU calls per dead-letter; (b) the taxonomy is inverted for timeouts: a transient Granite timeout on route docling_plus_granite_structured dead-letters on the first attempt while the identical timeout on docling_plus_structured_extraction (the default route the worker assigns at workers/extraction/worker.py:87-89) retries with backoff. The semantic worker similarly hardcodes retryable=True for all non-worker-contract exceptions. Quality outcomes themselves are correctly kept out of job failure (resolver outcomes persist in aggregate metadata and jobs complete), so the conflation is confined to runtime-failure classification.
lowerSeverity.evidence: model_failure_policy.py:21-25: `if isinstance(exc, ModelTimeoutError) and route_profile == "docling_plus_granite_structured": return ExtractionFailurePolicy(retryable=False, policy="do_not_retry_timeout")` then unconditional `retryable=True`. http_client.py:13 `class ModelRuntimeError(Exception): retryable = False` — `grep -rn '\.retryable' lib workers` shows the attribute is read nowhere. semantic worker:125-132 `except Exception as exc: jobs.fail_job(..., retryable=True, ...)`.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Base the policy on the exception contract: `retryable = getattr(exc, 'retryable', default)` with explicit overrides; make the Granite-timeout dead-letter decision route-independent (either all granite routes or none) and document why timeouts are non-retryable if GPU pile-up is the concern.

lowerSeverity.title: Profile registry drifts from compose/start-script server limits (Granite images 4 vs 1, visual-embed images 8 vs 1, Granite max_model_len unset vs 16384)

lowerSeverity.title: Live bring-up leaves the 'embeddings' queue with no worker and no service while extraction keeps enqueueing embed jobs
lowerSeverity.detail: phase8_5_live_bringup.sh starts profiles models-live/visual-embed-live/extraction/semantic/visual — never 'search' (worker-embeddings) or 'text-embed-live' (model-embed, which is also excluded from the models-live profile). lowerSeverity.title: Working-tree contract boundary fails open when the model-output schema cannot be loaded or is itself invalid
lowerSeverity.detail: The new fail-closed whole-payload validation (uncommitted) has two fail-open escape hatches: contract_root_payload returns the payload unvalidated with no rejected fields or errors when load_model_output_schema raises KeyError/OSError/ValueError or when the schema lacks a properties dict, and _contract_validation_errors returns [] (treated as fully valid) when Draft202012Validator.check_schema raises SchemaError. So a replayed envelope or direct caller carrying a stale/unknown model_output_schema_name skips the boundary entirely and reaches mapper logic unvalidated — exactly the compatibility/direct-call path the boundary exists to close. Risk is bounded because live adapters validate against the requested schema first and scripts/validate_contracts.py vets registered schemas in `make`-driven checks, but the boundary's own contract says fail-closed.

lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: When a non-None model_output_schema_name fails to resolve or its schema is invalid, return ({}, [], ["model_output_schema_unresolvable: <name>"]) so normalization records contract failure instead of mining the payload.

lowerSeverity.title: service_health_snapshots grows unbounded with no retention or supporting index for the admin latest-per-service query
lowerSeverity.detail: Every worker heartbeats record_service_health every ~30s (workers/*/worker.py), inserting a row per heartbeat; there is no DELETE/retention job anywhere and no index on (service_name, checked_at DESC), so the admin /service-health DISTINCT ON query sorts an ever-growing heap (~tens of thousands of rows/day across 8+ workers). Additionally the table CHECK constraint allows only ('ok','degraded','down','unknown') while the in-memory model snapshots use 'fixture' and 'unavailable' — harmless today only because model snapshots are never persisted, but it will reject inserts the moment someone wires probe persistence (which the health-surface fix above calls for).

lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Add an index on (service_name, checked_at DESC), a retention sweep (or UPSERT latest-per-service), and extend the status CHECK before persisting model probe statuses.

lowerSeverity.title: Transient retryable job failures mark documents pipeline_failed in analysis quality while a retry is still pending
lowerSeverity.detail: OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_STATUSES includes 'failed', and fail_job leaves a retryable job in status 'failed' (with scheduled_at = next_retry_at) between attempts. During that backoff window _operational_status reports the document as 'pipeline_failed', flipping Phase 9 eligibility to analysis_disabled_operational_failure even though the pipeline will retry and may complete cleanly. This is the one concrete spot where a transient job state is conflated with the terminal pipeline_failed quality outcome that ADR D8 reserves for runtime/system defects. Impact is a temporarily wrong quality/eligibility signal (it self-heals after a successful retry), but anything snapshotting document quality mid-run records the wrong outcome.
lowerSeverity.evidence: analysis_quality.py:14: `OPERATIONAL_FAILURE_STATUSES = {"failed", "dead_letter", "pipeline_failed"}`; service.py:405-407 sets status='failed' (not dead_letter) when attempts remain; analysis_quality.py:126-132 returns "pipeline_failed" for any job in those statuses on target queues.
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Treat 'failed' with attempts remaining as in-progress (e.g., only dead_letter/pipeline_failed are operational failures, or check error_json.retryable/next_retry_at) so pipeline_failed remains a terminal classification.

lowerSeverity.title: UI evidence selection still reads evidence[0] while the backend moved to deterministic evidence-locator selection
lowerSeverity.detail: ADR 0005's 2026-06-06 entries replaced every backend evidence[0] read with deterministic locator selection in lib/extraction/evidence_locator.py because 'equivalent provider evidence arrays' arrive reordered. The web client still hard-reads candidate.evidence[0] for both the jump-to-evidence target and the candidate card ('evidence page {candidate.evidence[0]?.pageNumber ?? "?"}'). When a candidate carries multiple evidence refs (page-only plus bbox/table-row), the UI may jump to and display the weakest locator, or a different one across runs, making the same canonical fact look differently anchored — the exact nondeterminism the backend change eliminated.

ADR 0005:515-518: 'Candidate admission fingerprints now select evidence locators deterministically instead of reading evidence[0].'
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Either have the API return a pre-selected primaryEvidence per candidate (computed with evidence_locator.py) or replicate the same richer-anchor-first selection in a shared web helper used by both the card and evidenceTargetFromCandidate.

lowerSeverity.title: Semantic canary scores the pre-normalization manifest while live Granite fanout consumes the family-repaired manifest
lowerSeverity.detail: The generalization spec makes the semantic-only canary 'the primary Qwen iteration gate' and requires it to score normalization-repair counts (eval item 11). The canary calls default_semantic_annotation_gateway().annotate() directly, so it evaluates raw structurally-normalized Qwen output; the live service then applies normalize_result_for_planning, which (per the family-repair finding) injects, rewrites, and drops regions before Granite fanout. As long as those repairs exist, the canary scorecard and the regions Granite actually receives diverge — region counts, semantic types, continuation/full-page metadata, and target schemas can all differ — so a passing canary does not validate live routing behavior, and repair volume is only indirectly inspectable via confidence.normalization keys (forbidden_normalization_keys) rather than scored counts.
lowerSeverity.evidence: run_phase8_5_semantic_canary.py:113 'result = default_semantic_annotation_gateway().annotate(source, quality_mode="smart")' with no normalize_result_for_planning; service.py:155 'manifest_result = normalize_result_for_planning(source, manifest_result)' only on the live path; scorecard has no repair-count metric (only forbidden_normalization_keys at line 440-444).
lowerSeverity.suggestedFix: Once family repairs are removed this divergence mostly disappears; until then, report both pre- and post-planning region sets in the canary JSON and add a scored normalization-repair-count check so injected/rewritten regions are visible at the gate.

A reviewer cannot distinguish real pipeline state from placeholder chrome.

The flag is still computed, persisted in page/document quality summaries, exposed as qwenRouteEligible in document API payloads, and declared in web types — implying a routing capability that no longer exists (it still also forces needs_review in classify_document, which may be intentional but is no longer Qwen-related). dimensionSummaries.summary: ADR 0005 is substantially implemented and the Implementation Progress log is accurate for D1-D4 and most of D6/D7: the vision adapter requires a JSON Schema, sends strict json_schema with no json_object path anywhere in the repo, validates returned JSON against the request schema and fails closed; Granite and Qwen gateways implement the retry-once-same-schema policy; Claims are anchor-required, typed-or-dropped, registry-gated, and Qwen is blocked at claim construction, candidate creation, and admission; a single registry-driven resolver applies source precedence, agreement, and registered arithmetic/line-item/upper-bound invariants; repeatability fingerprints hash the canonical projection and drift excludes rejectionDistribution. The significant remaining conformance gaps are: receipt is fully registered (D5) but has no aggregate reconciliation lane so receipts never get cross-region resolution, a canonical aggregate, or a quality outcome; D8 quality outcomes are persisted only inside aggregate normalized_json metadata with no DB column, no API/UI surface, an unreachable no_extraction_target branch, and a dead combine_quality_outcomes helper; the user-facing rerun_extraction review action enqueues a document-level extract job that live routing categorically rejects; and aggregate-level candidate creation still round-trips the projected payload through legacy non-Claim parsing, producing header candidates that are structurally guaranteed to be rejected for missing evidence because the claim projection drops anchors from header fields.

The Docling -> Qwen Smart Parse -> Granite -> Claims/resolver pipeline is largely wired as the ADR describes, but the trace surfaced several real seams at stage boundaries. The most serious is the reconciliation trigger: it compares completed region-extraction rows against a count of ALL extract jobs ever enqueued for the annotation regardless of job status, so a single dead-lettered or cancelled region job (and Granite timeouts dead-letter on the FIRST attempt via do_not_retry_timeout) permanently suppresses the document aggregate with no review signal. Receipt — a first-class registry family with declared aggregate projection metadata — is missing entirely from aggregate reconciliation, so cross-region receipt resolution, line-item-sum invariants, and canonical receipt payloads never run end-to-end. Claim/anchor identity includes semantic_region_id (off the ADR contract), which defeats cross-region dedupe and can duplicate line items in canonical aggregates when Qwen and Docling-structural regions overlap (region dedupe runs before granite_task repair, so overlap survives planning). Planner fanout caps (6 tasks/doc, 4 line-item tables, 3/page, 4 Docling structural targets) silently drop continuation line-item tables on longer documents, and the aggregate neither consumes the persisted plan-drop telemetry nor marks the output incomplete. Reconciliation is also not strictly exactly-once under concurrent workers, and the docling worker swallows semantic-annotation enqueue failures, stranding parsed documents.

The deterministic Claims pipeline is architecturally sound (anchor-required typing, method-first Qwen exclusion, deterministic sorting/hashing are all in place and tested), but I found one critical and several high-severity logic bugs that directly corrupt canonical output. Most damaging: line-item group identity treats region-level element_id/bbox as row identity, so contract-valid Granite output with null row_index collapses N distinct line items into one Frankenstein row (demonstrated end-to-end: 3 receipt rows -> 1 projected row). Money handling fabricates "USD" for every amount (no currency exists anywhere in the Granite contracts), and string-amount parsing mis-handles accounting negatives and comma-decimal locales by 100-1000x. The invoice aggregate wrapper fabricates totals.total from amount_paid, contradicting the resolver's own absent decision. Several smaller issues (missing-optional-treated-as-zero invariant demotions, non-ISO typed dates failing the canonical format:date contract, fail-open contract boundary on unknown schema names, no receipt aggregate path) erode determinism and review-precision rather than corrupting data. All 309 extraction unit tests pass, meaning none of these behaviors is covered by tests.

Of the ten quality risks flagged after the 20260501T080539Z corpus run, only one is cleanly FIXED in the working tree (semantic/document-family read-model alignment). Five are PARTIALLY fixed: cross-region duplicate identity, Granite echo defense, observation signal filtering, confidence coherence, and cross-window continuation handling each received real hardening on one layer (deterministic evidence-locator selection, strict fail-closed constrained decoding, candidate-level junk gates, confidence removal from resolver precedence) but leave a structural gap on the canonical-aggregate path, mostly because semantic_region_id is baked into Claim/anchor/group/dedupe identity and because the claim-resolver aggregate path bypasses the candidate-layer content gates. Four remain fully OPEN: expected-field-vs-actual telemetry, proactive Qwen input-budget warnings on the live path, intent-field persistence, and the routing gateway's STRUCTURED_SCHEMAS omission of document_observation (the last is latent/low-impact today). One new concrete defect was found while verifying risk 7: line-item group ordering sorts anchor JSON lexicographically, so rows/pages with indices >= 10 project out of physical order, contradicting the ADR progress log's "physical row order" claim.

The model-runtime layer is largely faithful to ADR 0005: fixture gateways are correctly gated behind STRUCTURA_MODEL_MODE (lib/extraction/gateways/routing.py:73, lib/semantic_annotations/service.py:373, lib/search/embedding_defaults.py:43-83), the vision adapter enforces strict json_schema with fail-closed retry-once semantics, contract validation (scripts/validate_contracts.py + lib/contracts/registry.py) enforces strict structured-output shape, and I verified no pending DB drift — every table/column the workers and Phase 8.5 harnesses reference exists through migration 085. The serious production gaps are operational: the live text-embedding path is broken against the compose-documented TEI service (wrong /embed payload shape plus an arch-pinned binary in the start script, currently masked because the live bring-up de-scopes text embeddings while workers keep enqueueing embed jobs into a consumer-less queue); the model health surface still does not persist probe results or record probed URLs (the June finding is unfixed) and cannot distinguish a placeholder or wrong model from the real service; and the job-layer failure taxonomy ignores the exception-level retryable contract, so deterministic protocol/config failures retry five times while Granite timeouts on one route dead-letter immediately. There is also quiet profile drift between lib/model_runtime/profiles.py and compose/start scripts (Granite and visual-embed image limits, Granite max_model_len), the configured Qwen semantic profile setting is ignored by the runtime gateway, and the Phase 8.5 spec/example env files still name env vars (STRUCTURA_MODEL_QWEN_URL, STRUCTURA_QWEN_PROFILE, MODEL_QWEN_PORT) that the code silently ignores. Quality outcomes vs job failures are mostly separated correctly (resolver outcomes persist as metadata, jobs complete), with the main conflation being timing-based: any 'failed' job awaiting retry marks the document pipeline_failed in analysis quality.

The Phase 8.5 semantic-planner contract surface is largely implemented as specified (12-region cap, all document/page/region telemetry fields, Granite fanout cap of 6 with line-item/summary protection and dedupe, Docling context anchor counts/family tension/weak-table markers, class-based few-shots, and a rich canary scorecard). The single biggest spec gap is that family-specific semantic-intent normalization — explicitly listed as "drift to remove" and a Definition-of-Done blocker in the generalization spec — is still active and has actually grown: manifest normalization synthesizes regions the model never emitted, rewrites semantic types, and injects requires_full_page_image/coverage_role for service-record, retail-order, receipt, real-estate-title, and medical-EOB families. On the UI/workflow side, the review queue is not dependable for Phase 8.5 output: quality outcomes and claim-resolver decisions/reason codes are persisted but exposed by no API route; observation_review/line_item_review/relationship_suggestion tasks render with no candidate values or evidence and cannot be accepted; and the "Re-run extraction" review action enqueues a document-level Granite job that the live routing gateway now fails closed by design. The Viewer's evidence surface always renders page 1 with a fabricated fallback highlight, undermining the jump-to-evidence trust loop, and several review/inbox surfaces still show hard-coded placeholder data ("86% confidence", zeroed pipeline stages) and stale Phase-8 concepts (qwenRouteEligible, escalation fields).
